name: JW Marriott New Orleans
positioning: Canal Street hotel in the French Quarter with a rooftop saltwater pool, bi-level suites and a two-story Executive Lounge
best_for: Travelers who want a Canal Street base near Bourbon Street and the St. Louis Cathedral
Families and groups wanting two-bedroom or bi-level suites

facts.text: The hotel is located on Canal Street in the French Quarter.
The outdoor pool is heated, and towels are provided.
The hotel has a 24-hour fitness center.
Guest rooms offer chic designs and plush bedding.
Some deluxe guest rooms have French Quarter views, and some larger Premium rooms have Canal Street views.
The Executive Lounge has a library, a pool table, flat-screen TVs and a family room, with a deluxe continental breakfast, coffee, tea, snacks and non-alcoholic drinks daily.
Fogo de Chao, the hotel's Brazilian steakhouse, serves churrasco steaks in a smart-casual setting.
The Lobby Lounge cocktail bar serves creative cocktails, shareable plates and entrees.
The hotel has an indoor and outdoor event venue with a balcony overlooking Canal Street.
The concierge can help arrange tours and point guests toward nearby landmarks like Bourbon Street and the St. Louis Cathedral.
The Shops at Canal Place are three blocks from the hotel.
On-property activations include poetry performances, cooking demonstrations and art exhibits.

highlights.text: The hotel has a rooftop saltwater pool.

JW Marriott's Epicurean Journey offers daily culinary and cultural experiences inspired by New Orleans, such as encounters with local poets, artists and storytellers, or warm beignets and cafe au lait.
Two-bedroom suites give groups room to spread out, including bi-level layouts with extra living space; the bi-level suites suit families.
The redesigned suites have marble bathrooms, and the accommodations offer a calm retreat above the busy streets.

considerations.text: The minimum age to check in is 21.
Parking is by on-site valet, and pets are not allowed.
WhataHotel notes the French Quarter location can be bustling and crowded.
